title: Morgue: a wall of body drawers and slab tables
what: A low basement room whose walls are entirely steel body drawers in a grid, with concrete slab tables in the floor each holding a corpse, a few ceiling vent-lights, blood-spattered tile floor. One drawer is a separate, scratched sprite. A corridor leads off to a room where a body hangs from chains. First second: the drawer grid, the corpses on slabs, the low ceiling.
recipe: Host s218 is 9216 x 9216 units (15.6 m), 2.96 bodies high, 7 bodies below the ground floor; floor 296 (owner: grimy tiles), ceiling 416. The drawer wall is tile 311 (64x128 px, two drawer doors per tile, 1.93 bodies per repeat, used on 19 walls); single scratched drawer doors are wall sprites of tile 325 (7 of them, type 417). Slab tables are separate sectors of 1536 x 768 (2.6 x 1.3 m) walled in 272 (grey concrete), tops at differing heights (s327/s329/s330/s332 etc.), with corpse/gib sprites (2077 type 18) on them. Lights: tile 501 sprites (technical light).
use: The basement of the edge hospital, or the back of a funeral home: one stair or lift down from a ground-floor corridor. The player searches slabs for a key, and an opened drawer (a drawer sprite on a slide) can hide a secret or spill a zombie.
